Stated Claim / Post Context:
Shane Gillis' ex-girlfriend mercilessly mocks comedian after 'misogynistic' SNL monologue

Brassel poked fun at his controversial Saturday Night Live monologue in a series of Instagram posts. The former couple, who began dating in July 2024, parted ways last year.

Actual Article Body:
By SONIA HORON, US ASSISTANT SHOWBIZ EDITOR

Published:  10:32 AEDT, 16 October 2026   |  Updated:  13:12 AEDT, 16 October 2026

Shane Gillis' ex-girlfriend Grace Brassel poked fun at his controversial Saturday Night Live monologue in a series of Instagram posts.

While guest-hosting the latest episode of SNL, the comedian, 38, performed a bit in which he remarked that female gymgoers 'just dress like w****s now.'

On Wednesday, Brassel shared a video of herself at the gym, with a text overlay on top that read, 'Full Body Workout for H*es.'

'Here's my super quick full body workout as a big old h*e at the gym,' she joked in a voiceover at the start of the clip. 'Alright, come on guys, we can have fun here,' she said, before going over her gym routine.

At the end she added, 'Be a young h*e and run free. Have fun at the gym.'

Brassel also reposted a video of Dan Levy lambasting Gillis for his 'misogynistic' joke to her Instagram Stories on Tuesday, before writing, 'ANYWAYS… y’all need anything from the store?'

Shane Gillis', 38, ex-girlfriend Grace Brassel poked fun at his controversial Saturday Night Live monologue in a series of Instagram posts

While guest-hosting the latest episode of SNL, the comedian performed a bit in which he remarked that female gymgoers 'just dress like w****s now'

She later shared a gym selfie with the caption 'Fitcheck!'

The Daily Mail has reached out to Gillis' representative for comment.

The former couple, who began dating in July 2024, parted ways in 2025.

Last week, Brassel spoke out about their romance in another Instagram video, revealing that the relationship 'fully stripped me of who I am.'

The video featured a montage of clips, including a number that saw her crying, before shifting to happier moments after the breakup.

'Last year I was in a relationship that fully stripped me of who I am. I’ve been so terrified to even talk about what I went through, especially after relentless bullying from his fanbase (for no reason),' she wrote in the caption.

'I want to share this to let women know IT GETS BETTER!! And you can do it! I had it on level hard mode and I survived! And I’ve never been happier.❤️'

'I know that his fans are going to purposefully misunderstand me; I’m used to it. I have videos of me crying because I used it as a video diary for myself,' she went on.

'I never thought I would share them. The main point of this video is for people to know there’s more to life… regardless if my ex is a famous comedian or not. I want to show there’s hope. Sending love to you all. ❤️'

'You are so much more than someone's girlfriend,' she wrote in a text overlay on the video.

The post was set to Ashe's 2026 hit song Stop The Wedding!

Numerous celebrities, including Martha Plimpton, have taken aim at the comic and SNL creator Lorne Michaels, 81, following his widely derided appearance on the show over the weekend.

Gillis described women's activewear as 'neon' and 'artificial bait-colored' with wrinkles that 'go around the cheeks and all combine at the butthole.'

He quipped: 'And don’t look. You’re not allowed to look. For real, don’t look, because they are filming. I’m in the background of like 10 TikToks right now.'

He quickly drew howls of condemnation on X, where one user branded him 'a d*****bag frat bro' and another called him a 'disgusting man.'

East of Eden star Plimpton, 55, blasted Gillis's opener as 'stupid' in an Instagram video on Tuesday.

'There's this Shane Gillis guy who I've never heard of who said some really f***ing stupid s*** live on air on SNL on Saturday,' Plimpton began.

'It's like really stupid s**t. He deserves a spanking from his mama,' Plimpton said.

Plimpton then hit out at SNL creator Michaels for surrounding himself with 'all white men.'

Among those catching strays amid the fury at Gillis was Travis Kelce, as social media erupted with outrage after fans spotted that the NFL star had liked a post featuring Gillis's monologue.

Kelce, 37, who married Taylor Swift this summer at a ceremony officiated by Adam Sandler, liked the video of the set shared on the series' official Instagram page.

As a social media furor erupted over the monologue, Gillis was also vociferously denounced in an Instagram video by Schitt's Creek star Dan Levy.

'Women wearing short shorts at the gym does not make them w****s. It makes the men calling them w****s misogynists. There’s a difference there,' said Levy.

Saturday Night Live alumna Ego Nwodim also responded as she posted a mirror selfie she snapped at the gym, accompanied by the caption: 'w**** reporting for duty'

Should comedians be held accountable for jokes that offend or demean women on national TV?

'By the way, I've seen more men's nipples at the gym than I've ever seen women showing their bodies off,' observed the son of SCTV icon Eugene Levy.

'But I'm speechless that something like that can exist on live national television. And to be perfectly honest, more men need to be standing up in opposition to this, because it's complacency that has created the environment with which women are sexually assaulted and it's a "conversation" as opposed to a crime.'

SNL alumna Ego Nwodim, who was a cast member on the show for seven seasons from 2018 to 2025, retorted to Gillis with jokes of her own.

She fired up her Insta Stories and posted a mirror selfie at the gym with one arm raised, accompanied by the caption: 'w**** reporting for duty.'

Gillis made headlines in 2019 when he was hired to join the cast of SNL, only to be fired over resurfaced podcast clips of his politically incorrect comic bits, including one in which he used the ethnic slur 'ch**k.'

Since Gillis was hired at the same time as Bowen Yang, the first SNL cast member of Asian descent, the jokes elicited an even stronger reaction.

Gillis issued a statement noting he is a 'comedian who pushes boundaries,' while offering 'to apologize to anyone who's actually offended by anything I've said.'

In the ensuing years, Gillis rose back to showbiz success, and by 2023 he released a stand-up special that made the Netflix Top 10 in five countries.
